chunks: And in the narration of Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab and Khaṭṭab Abu Muhammad al-Hamdani, from Ṭirbal, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, that he said:

Indeed, the woman does not inherit from what her husband leaves behind of villages, houses, weapons, and animals; and she inherits from wealth, slaves, clothing, and the household goods from what he leaves behind.
Then he said: And the dismantled materials of trunks, reeds, and doors are appraised, and she is given her rightful share from it.

key_terms.الرَّقِيقِ: slaves or bondpersons counted among inheritable property
key_terms.الْقُرَى وَالدُّورِ: villages and houses as categories of estate property
key_terms.الْمَالِ: wealth or monetary property from which inheritance is taken
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةَ: the wife as inheriting party in this ruling
key_terms.نِقْضُ الْأَجْذَاعِ وَالْقَصَبِ وَالْأَب: dismantled building materials whose value is assessed

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about a wife's inheritance from her husband's property?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling on a wife's inheritance from her husband's estate, distinguishing between categories of property from which she does and does not inherit. It also states that certain structural materials are to be appraised so that her due share may be given from their value.
